question: Where can I get a list of hydrogen production plants (electrolysers) in operation in the United States, with location, capacity (MW), operator and commissioning date?

answer.summary: Best source is DOE Hydrogen Program Record 24001 (May 2024): 113 existing and planned US electrolyzer rows, 70 installed rows totalling about 116 MW (largest Woodbine GA, 40 MW), with city, kW and status only. It names no operator and gives no commissioning date; those came from company documents for two sites (Plug Power Woodbine, FPL Okeechobee). IEA's June 2026 project database needs an account and was not opened. Newer plants are missing from DOE's edition.
main_caveats: DOE Record 24001 is dated May 2024 and is still the newest electrolyzer-installations record on DOE's program page; later plants and status changes are missing.
Table 1 gives kW per installation row without stating the electrical or output basis; hydrogen output (for example 15 tons per day at Woodbine) is a different measure.
No operator or commissioning date in the DOE table; 'Installed' rows include 46 units of 120-180 kW and 4 'Commissioning' rows, so installed is not proof of operation.
Woodbine GA appears three times (40 MW and 5 MW operational, 40 MW planned); rows are installations, not unique plants.
IEA's June 2026 database and Clean Energy Group's April 2025 map were not inspected beyond their pages; Plug Power's own release page blocks automated clients.
answer.confidence_reason: Table counts reconcile with DOE's totals and two sites were traced to operator releases, but the list is 18 months old and the IEA file and most operators were not checked.

attributes.note: DOE Table 1 gives city and state per installation (28 of 70 installed rows state only); no coordinates. Operator releases name the site for two plants.
attributes.gap_note: Coordinates and street addresses were not found; IEA's file (location fields unknown) needs an account.

attributes.note: DOE gives kW per row (70 installed rows, 115,980 kW; basis not stated); releases give 8 x 5 MW (Plug) and 25 MW (FPL). Tons per day is a separate measure.
attributes.gap_note: The electrical or output basis of DOE's kW is not stated and was not verified against operator documents beyond two sites.

attributes.note: DOE Table 1 omits operators by design; only two per-site documents (Plug Power, Florida Power & Light) name one. No list with operators was found.
attributes.gap_note: Operators for the other 11 installed sites of 1 MW or more and for the small units were not checked; IEA's database may list developers but needs an account.

attributes.note: DOE labels status (Installed/Operational, Installed/Commissioning) without dates. Releases give Jan 2024 (Plug) and Oct 2023 first hydrogen / Feb 2024 completion (FPL).
attributes.gap_note: Dates for all other installations were not found; no source states the date of continuous operation.

sources.name: DOE Hydrogen Program Record 24001, Electrolyzer Installations in the United States (Table 1)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Energy, Hydrogen Program (HFTO)
sources.format: PDF (Table 1 extractable with pdftotext -layout; map as figure)
sources.summary: Table of 113 existing and planned US electrolyzer rows (May 2024): 70 installed rows with 115,980 kW, 13 of them 1 MW or more (largest Woodbine GA 40 MW); location, kW and status only.

example.example_request: curl -sL -o rec24001.pdf https://www.hydrogen.energy.gov/docs/hydrogenprogramlibraries/pdfs/24001-electrolyzer-installations-united-states.pdf ; pdftotext -layout rec24001.pdf rec24001.txt ; keep lines of Table 1 matching '<location>  <kW>  <status>' (three columns separated by two or more spaces).
example.example_result: 113 rows, 4,523,985 kW in total. Installed: 70 rows, 115,980 kW. Example rows: 'Woodbine, GA 40,000 Installed/Operational'; 'Okeechobee, FL 25,000 Installed/Commissioning'; 'Donaldsonville, LA 20,000 Installed/Commissioning'.

members_summary.pattern: Search '<operator> <city> electrolyzer commissioning' on the operator newsroom; utilities and gas suppliers announce start-ups.
